items.title: Frank Amacker Interview, 1960-07-01
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...he was making records with Joe Dierensburg. ... [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah.

ctx.x: Look a fella out there. I run into a fella out there. Some of the best piano players I'd ever heard. The man out there now, if he's still alive, by the name of Harvey Brooks.
Oh yeah, he's still going. Yeah, you know, did you have him? Sure, he was making records with Joe Dierensburg. Oh. You know that Yellow Dog Blues that was a hit? Yeah. That was him on piano, then.

Yeah. And the little boy told me. That's his name, the little boy told me. Yeah. Another fella called a fella out there, a very popular fella, in the musical world, by the name of Elsie Cooper. Elsie Cooper is Harvey Brooks. And Walter Johnson was a very popular, because he passed. Walter Johnson was a crackerjack player while he lived. I don't believe you got me now. Yeah. He was a crackerjack player, Walter Johnson and Harold Brown. Walter Johnson and Harold Brown, they were crackerjacks in that day. And, um,…
